key_insight: A general-purpose language model can directly write a small neural network’s weights to rank material candidates without property labels and improve early-stage discovery.
engineering_relevance: These label-free predictors can initialize surrogate models and screen generated crystals when measurements or simulations are scarce.
method: Provide the language model with a task description, input names, and a zero-initialized network with 16 hidden units.
Have it fill in every weight using learned materials knowledge.
Use the network for ranking, as a Bayesian model’s prior mean, or to screen crystal-generator outputs.
evidence_signal: Zero-label Spearman correlations reached 0.64–0.79 on experimental alloys and 0.95 on generated crystals; Bayesian optimization regret fell significantly on 4 of 5 experimental tasks.
watch_item: Benefits are concentrated in the first tens of labels and on targets not already well ranked by simple rules or subsystem extrapolation.
